title: Learning a second language
text: Learning a second language have many benefits. Many adults believe that they are too old learning a new language, but research suggests that age is not the most importance factor. What matters more is how often do people practise. I started learning English in the age of twelve, but I made slow progress at school. Two years ago, I move to Melbourne to study. Since then, my speaking has improved quickly. Because I use English every day. My advice to other learners is simple: find real reasons to use the language, and practise a little every day.

errors.ruleReminder: An -ing subject (learning a language) is singular and takes a singular verb.
errors.explanation: The subject is learning a second language, one activity, so the verb is has.

errors.ruleReminder: After too + adjective, use to + verb: too old to learn.
errors.explanation: The pattern is too + adjective + to + verb, so we need to learn.

errors.ruleReminder: Before a noun, use an adjective: the most important factor.
errors.explanation: Importance is a noun. Before factor, we need the adjective important.

errors.ruleReminder: In a question inside a sentence, use statement order: subject + verb. Do not use do or does.
errors.explanation: Inside a sentence, how often people practise uses statement order, so do is removed.

errors.ruleReminder: Use at with ages: at the age of twelve, at 18.
errors.explanation: The fixed phrase is at the age of, not in the age of.

errors.ruleReminder: Use the past simple for finished past events (two years ago).
errors.explanation: Two years ago is a finished time, so the verb must be past simple: moved.

errors.ruleReminder: A because clause cannot be a sentence on its own. Join it to the main clause.
errors.explanation: Because I use English every day is not a full sentence. Join it to the sentence before.
